title: Fantastic Four
subtitle: Marvel’s First Family: foundational stories, modern starts, and the Hickman saga.
intro: Start with Waid and Wieringo for a modern family introduction, Ryan North for a later entry, or Lee and Kirby for the original foundation. Hickman’s Fantastic Four/FF adds Reed, Doom, and family background to Secret Wars (2015); it is useful optional reading, while Avengers/New Avengers supplies the direct event buildup.

stories.title: The Fantastic Four begins
stories.why: The family’s original adventures and first major foes.
stories.match: Choose Masterworks Vol. 1 for #1–10 or the larger World’s Greatest Comic Magazine Epic for #1–18. These overlap.

stories.title: The Galactus Trilogy
stories.match: Masterworks Vol. 5 includes #41–50. The Coming of Galactus Epic includes #33–51 and also covers the next entry.

stories.title: This Man… This Monster!
stories.match: Masterworks Vol. 6 begins at #51; the Coming of Galactus Epic also includes it. Do not borrow overlapping editions unnecessarily.

stories.title: John Byrne: Back to the Basics
stories.why: A classic new creative-run starting point.
stories.match: Visionaries John Byrne Vol. 1 and Masterworks Vol. 21 both cover #232–240. Choose one.

stories.title: The Trial of Reed Richards
stories.match: Visionaries John Byrne Vol. 4 covers #258–267. The issue is cover-dated January 1984; preceding Galactus stories provide context.

stories.title: Waid & Wieringo: Imaginauts
stories.why: A widely recommended modern family introduction.
stories.match: Ultimate Collection Book 1 includes the opening; Imaginauts is another edition. Ultimate Collection is a format label, not the Ultimate universe.

stories.title: Unthinkable
stories.why: A major Doctor Doom story after Imaginauts.
stories.match: Both Unthinkable collections list #67–70 and #500–502, including the arc and aftermath. Choose either edition.

stories.title: Jonathan Hickman’s Fantastic Four / FF saga
stories.issues: Dark Reign: Fantastic Four #1–5; Fantastic Four #570–588, #600–611 and #605.1; FF (2011) #1–23
stories.why: An ambitious family-and-cosmic saga; useful optional background for Secret Wars.
stories.match: These are consecutive parts, not alternatives: Complete Collections 1–3 cover Dark Reign, Fantastic Four #570–588/#600–604 and FF #1–16; finish with Fantastic Four by Hickman Vol. 6 (#605,605.1,606–611) and FF Vol. 4 (#17–23). The two series interleave: follow the linked issue order. Solve Everything alone covers only #570–588, not the full saga.

stories.title: Secret Wars (2015)
stories.why: A later payoff for Reed, Doom, and Hickman’s broader Marvel saga.
stories.match: This is the 2015 event, not the twelve-issue 1984 Marvel Super Heroes Secret Wars. Avengers/New Avengers and Time Runs Out form the direct lead-in; Fantastic Four/FF is optional background.

stories.title: Ryan North: Whatever Happened to the Fantastic Four?
stories.why: A later entry built around the family and inventive science-fiction problems.
stories.match: This starts North’s 2022 series. Save Everyone begins his separate 2025 relaunch and is not the same Vol. 1.
